title: College Football Top 25 State of the Programs
description: A sourced snapshot of the 2026 season for the 25 teams in the October 4 AP poll, with a separate Coaches comparison, latest results, next games and original editorial analysis.
headline: Texas leads as October brings the next big tests
dek: Georgia at Alabama and UCLA at Oregon headline a week that can clarify an unsettled national picture.

ranking_guide.ap: Media-voted ranking. The program list follows the AP order, reproduced by NCAA.com for the October 4 release.
ranking_guide.coaches: Separate ranking by participating coaches. A null rank means the team is outside that poll's Top 25; the two affected AP teams received votes.
ranking_guide.editorial: The status labels, season interpretation, why_here and watch_next fields are original editorial analysis based on the linked results. They are not an official explanation of any voter’s ballot.
ranking_guide.predictive: Predictive ratings estimate future team strength. No dated, current numeric model rating was verified for this edition. Numeric rating fields are intentionally absent.
ranking_guide.playoff: AP and Coaches positions are not CFP committee rankings or playoff seeds.

overview.heading: The top holds while the middle moves
overview.text: Texas leads the October 4 AP poll after a weekend off, and the first five places are unchanged. The larger story sits underneath: Missouri’s rout of Florida reshuffled the SEC’s middle, Pittsburgh turned an unbeaten start into a ranking, and several teams slipped despite winning. October now offers a useful change of pace. Georgia visits Alabama, UCLA visits Oregon, and Indiana travels to unbeaten Nebraska. Those games should provide stronger comparisons than another week of arguing over small poll movements.

overview.heading: Texas has earned the position and still has work ahead
overview.text:
The Longhorns’ opening four games include a 24-23 win over Ohio State and a 20-17 win at Tennessee. That is real evidence against capable opposition, although the narrow margins also leave room for challengers. Oklahoma is next in Dallas, followed by Florida and Ole Miss. For Texas, the question is whether a team that has already handled pressure can start creating more breathing room.

Georgia and Alabama arrive at their meeting unbeaten and 3-0 in the SEC. Georgia’s 38-14 win over Vanderbilt featured a decisive defensive adjustment: the Commodores gained only 61 yards after halftime. Alabama has scored at least 45 points in every game and just put 56 on Mississippi State. Its four takeaways helped make that result lopsided. The matchup asks a straightforward question: can Georgia disrupt Alabama’s rhythm without leaving its own offense in a race?

overview.heading: The SEC offers evidence in both directions
overview.text:
Missouri supplied the weekend’s clearest correction. A week after losing at Mississippi State, the Tigers beat Florida 45-17, their largest margin over a top-10 opponent. Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards, and Missouri scored 35 consecutive points. The result supports renewed attention; a follow-up against Texas A&M will test whether it was the start of a sustained change.

Florida’s last two Saturdays explain the difficulty of sorting the conference. The Gators beat Ole Miss 52-28, then lost by 28 themselves. Ole Miss still owns a win over LSU, while Mississippi State owns a win over Missouri. Tennessee sits nearby with a three-point loss to Texas and a ground-led recovery against Auburn. LSU’s 731 yards against McNeese were impressive production, but Kentucky on the road will provide a more useful comparison. A single head-to-head result helps; this collection of results resists a tidy ordering.

overview.heading: The Big Ten has two races taking shape
overview.text:
Ohio State and Indiana remain close to the national lead. The Buckeyes’ only loss came by one point at Texas, and they outgained Iowa 484-238 in their latest win. Indiana answered a close Northwestern game by producing 593 yards against Rutgers. Josh Hoover has 15 touchdown passes and no interceptions this season. Indiana’s trip to Nebraska comes before the October 17 meeting with Ohio State, so looking ahead would be costly.

Oregon and UCLA offer a different kind of comparison. The Ducks recovered from their Oklahoma State loss with wins over Portland State and USC. UCLA is 4-0 after beating Cal, San Diego State, Purdue and Maryland. Autzen should reveal more about the Bruins’ ceiling while giving Oregon another substantial chance to rebuild its résumé. USC, meanwhile, needed a comeback from 21-10 down to beat Washington. Iowa’s offense managed only 39 rushing yards against Ohio State. Both have immediate road tests, at Penn State and Washington respectively.

overview.heading: The Big 12 keeps its unbeaten options open
overview.text:
BYU, Texas Tech and Utah have yet to lose. Their latest evidence looks quite different. BYU escaped a wet night at TCU with a 17-10 victory, helped by four sacks and a late Bear Bachmeier touchdown. Texas Tech trailed Colorado at halftime before four interceptions helped turn the game into a 29-7 win. Utah returns from its open date with four wins, including a 31-17 result at Iowa State.

The next useful checkpoints are close: BYU hosts Iowa State on Friday and Notre Dame a week later. Utah hosts Kansas before later meetings with Houston and BYU. Texas Tech has a week off before Arizona State. Oklahoma State remains one of the most difficult teams to place, with a loss at Tulsa followed by a win over Oregon. Houston’s 27 unanswered points against UCF kept its one-loss season alive, but the early deficit is something to fix before Kansas State.

overview.heading: Watch the programs earning a longer look
overview.text:
Notre Dame stayed unbeaten with a 37-26 road win at North Carolina and hosts Stanford before traveling to BYU. Miami’s 41-13 win at Clemson was more decisive: six sacks, just 55 rushing yards allowed, and a third ACC road victory. The Hurricanes get an open week before Florida State.

At the other end of the poll, Pittsburgh earned entry after a 35-33 Friday win at Virginia Tech. SMU beat Boston College with only 218 yards of offense, while Boise State opened Pac-12 conference play by beating Utah State 37-18. These are useful results with different implications. Pitt has an unbeaten record to defend; SMU needs cleaner offense; Boise State now has a road conference test at Fresno State.

overview.heading: How to read the numbers
overview.text: This feature uses the AP order as its index and shows the Coaches Poll separately. AP voters are journalists and broadcasters; the Coaches Poll represents participating coaches. They can differ substantially: Indiana is fifth with the coaches and seventh in AP, while Oklahoma State and Boise State are outside the Coaches Top 25. Predictive systems such as ESPN’s FPI estimate future strength. The program labels and assessments here are editorial analysis of verified results. No current numerical predictive rating was verified for this edition, so none is displayed. AP and Coaches positions should not be read as playoff seeding.

programs.season_so_far: Wins over Ohio State and Tennessee carry the unbeaten record. Both were one-possession games, so the résumé is stronger than the margins are comfortable.
programs.why_here: The poll lead rests on meaningful wins. October's SEC run will show how much separation Texas really has.
programs.watch_next: Red River in Dallas begins a stretch that includes Florida and Ole Miss.

programs.season_so_far: Georgia is 3-0 in the SEC. Against Vanderbilt, Gunner Stockton supplied 295 passing yards and three touchdown passes; the defense allowed 61 yards after halftime.
programs.why_here: A strong second-half response kept the start clean. Alabama supplies a much harder test of the same formula.
programs.watch_next: Can Georgia slow Alabama's scoring pace in Tuscaloosa?

programs.season_so_far: The Irish returned from a rain-soaked North Carolina trip with a 37-26 win and a fifth straight victory to open the season.
programs.why_here: Winning consecutive road games sustains the case near the top. The coming trip to BYU is the more revealing measuring stick.
programs.watch_next: Handle Stanford before the Oct. 17 visit to BYU.

programs.season_so_far: Miami is 3-0 in conference after road wins at Stanford, Wake Forest and Clemson. Six sacks and 55 rushing yards allowed powered the latest win.
programs.why_here: The defense made the Clemson result convincing. Sustaining that physical advantage is the key to the next phase.
programs.watch_next: A bye precedes the home rivalry game.

programs.season_so_far: The lone defeat was 24-23 at Texas. Ohio State has won three straight, most recently outgaining Iowa 484-238 in a 31-14 road victory.
programs.why_here: The Iowa performance supports a strong one-loss résumé. The Indiana game can change the Big Ten hierarchy.
programs.watch_next: Maryland comes first; at Indiana follows Oct. 17.

programs.season_so_far: Alabama has reached 45 points in all five games. The Mississippi State win combined 483 yards with four takeaways and only 18 rushing yards allowed.
programs.why_here: The first ranked win was emphatic. Georgia will test how much of that dominance transfers to a top opponent.
programs.watch_next: A 5-0 versus 5-0 showdown, followed by Tennessee on the road.

programs.season_so_far: Indiana extended its winning streak to 21 games. Josh Hoover has 15 touchdown passes without an interception; the Rutgers win produced 593 yards.
programs.why_here: Dropping a poll spot after a 32-point win says more about a crowded top tier than a stumble. Nebraska and Ohio State raise the difficulty.
programs.watch_next: An unbeaten opponent in Lincoln, then Ohio State at home Oct. 17.

programs.season_so_far: BYU stayed unbeaten in a wet road game at TCU. Four sacks and a late Bear Bachmeier touchdown helped secure the one-score win.
programs.why_here: The record is valuable; the narrow escape leaves offensive questions. The next two home games offer a clearer read.
programs.watch_next: Friday night against Iowa State, then Notre Dame on Oct. 17.

programs.season_so_far: A 32-24 win over LSU preceded a 52-28 loss at Florida. The Rebels had a bye before returning to SEC play.
programs.why_here: The LSU result keeps the résumé relevant, but the Florida loss demands a defensive response.
programs.watch_next: Respond in Nashville before Missouri and Texas arrive on the schedule.

programs.season_so_far: LSU generated 731 yards in a 63-14 win over McNeese. Its earlier loss at Ole Miss remains the key blemish.
programs.why_here: The scoring surge is encouraging; the road conference test will tell more than the McNeese margin.
programs.watch_next: A trip to Lexington provides the next meaningful check.

programs.season_so_far: The Red Raiders trailed Colorado 7-3 at halftime but won 29-7, intercepting four passes. They have started 5-0 for a second consecutive season.
programs.why_here: The defense rescued a slow start. Cleaner offensive halves would make the unbeaten case more convincing.
programs.watch_next: The open week is followed by Arizona State in Lubbock.

programs.season_so_far: Utah's four wins include Arkansas 43-10, Utah State 33-0 and Iowa State 31-17. The Utes were off Oct. 3.
programs.why_here: The early scoring margins and a conference road win provide a solid base. The league schedule will deepen the evidence.
programs.watch_next: Kansas next; Houston on Oct. 24 and BYU on Nov. 7 are later checkpoints.

programs.season_so_far: The Ducks lost 39-31 at Oklahoma State, then beat Portland State and USC. Their last outing was a 41-27 win in Los Angeles.
programs.why_here: The USC response matters more than the idle-week rise. Unbeaten UCLA gives Oregon another chance to strengthen its standing.
programs.watch_next: Two rested teams meet at Autzen; Nebraska visits the following week.

programs.season_so_far: Missouri answered its Mississippi State loss by beating Florida 45-17. Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards; the Tigers scored 35 consecutive points.
programs.why_here: The dramatic rebound warrants attention. Repeating the performance is the question after two very different SEC Saturdays.
programs.watch_next: A second straight home game can establish whether the Florida result is a turning point.

programs.season_so_far: After losing 20-17 to Texas, Tennessee beat Auburn 24-14. DeSean Bishop supplied 220 rushing yards and all three touchdowns.
programs.why_here: A strong rushing response kept the season moving. More balanced production would ease the burden in the next SEC stretch.
programs.watch_next: Arkansas on the road precedes Alabama in Knoxville.

programs.season_so_far: Florida followed a 52-28 win over Ole Miss with a 45-17 loss at Missouri. Its record remains 4-1, with both quality and volatility visible.
programs.why_here: One bad afternoon does not erase the Ole Miss win, but the size of the reversal makes consistency the central issue.
programs.watch_next: A response is needed before the Oct. 17 trip to Texas.

programs.season_so_far: The Bulldogs beat Minnesota, South Carolina and Missouri before Alabama handed them their first defeat, 56-23.
programs.why_here: The earlier wins give the start substance. Recovering from Alabama's run-defense and turnover pressure is the immediate task.
programs.watch_next: An open week precedes the trip to Baton Rouge.

programs.season_so_far: A 24-10 opening loss at Tulsa was followed by wins over Oregon, Murray State and West Virginia. The Cowboys were idle Oct. 3.
programs.why_here: The Oregon win and Tulsa loss pull the evaluation in opposite directions. Continued conference wins can reduce that uncertainty.
programs.watch_next: UCF next, then a ranked Houston team on the road.

programs.season_so_far: USC rebounded from its Oregon loss by rallying from 21-10 down to beat Washington 25-21.
programs.why_here: The comeback preserved a strong record while leaving questions about complete-game control.
programs.watch_next: A road game in Penn State's White Out environment is the next test.

programs.season_so_far: Iowa's unbeaten start ended against Ohio State. The Hawkeyes managed 238 total yards and 39 rushing yards in the 31-14 loss.
programs.why_here: The loss exposed the challenge against a top offense and defensive front. The response matters more than the six-place slide.
programs.watch_next: Rebuild offensive traction on the road in Seattle.

programs.season_so_far: The Bruins beat Cal, San Diego State, Purdue and Maryland, scoring 54 in their last outing. They enter Oregon after a bye.
programs.why_here: The unbeaten start is clear; Oregon is a substantially stronger test of what those four wins mean nationally.
programs.watch_next: The ranked matchup at Autzen is the defining opportunity so far.

programs.season_so_far: Houston erased a 17-0 third-quarter deficit with 27 unanswered points against UCF. Conner Weigman ran for three touchdowns.
programs.why_here: The response showed resilience, but repeated slow starts would be expensive in the approaching stretch.
programs.watch_next: Kansas State begins a run that includes Oklahoma State and Utah.

programs.season_so_far: The Broncos beat Utah State 37-18 in their first Pac-12 conference game. A 21-0 start and six sacks helped establish control.
programs.why_here: The conference transition began well. Road results will be central to keeping a national ranking.
programs.watch_next: Fresno State is the next conference road test.

programs.season_so_far: SMU beat Boston College 25-16 in rain despite finishing with 218 total yards. The Mustangs have won twice since losing at Louisville.
programs.why_here: The defense helped protect the result. More efficient offense is the clearest route to a firmer ranking.
programs.watch_next: An open week precedes Virginia, followed by Cal at home.

programs.season_so_far: Pitt reached 5-0 by winning 35-33 at Virginia Tech on Friday. Earlier wins included UCF and Syracuse.
programs.why_here: The first road win strengthened an unbeaten résumé enough to reach the poll. Staying ranked requires turning the entry into a run.
programs.watch_next: North Carolina next; a visit to Miami follows Oct. 24.

data_quality.verified: Poll ranks and records checked against the dated NCAA AP table and AFCA Coaches table. Latest results and next opponents were checked against official school recaps or schedules.
data_quality.schedule_note: Games listed are the next scheduled game, not necessarily this weekend. Dates and kickoff times can change. Times shown in games_to_watch are converted to Pacific from official schedules.
source_cautions: A third-party poll archive disagreed with the primary AP/NCAA reporting on Missouri and Tennessee ordering and several point totals. It was excluded from the ranking baseline.
Some cached official schedule pages lagged completed results. Dated recaps and current primary poll records were used to resolve the current snapshot.
Pittsburgh's Virginia Tech win was Friday, October 2.
Boise State is a Pac-12 program in this 2026 snapshot.
No photographs, team logos, full articles or third-party text excerpts are included.
